page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by 16 physical cores of the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture operating at 3.4 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core and features an L3 cache capacity of 128 MB. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Local ephemeral storage is integrated directly via a 945 GB NVMe solid-state drive. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPU is not present on this server type.

Benchmark testing indicates distinct strengths in memory subsystem throughput. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth at 307.54 GB/sec and memory write bandwidth at 124.58 GB/sec, corroborated by a strong PassMark memory score of 2945.61. Single-threaded gzip compression is also upper-quartile at 33.08 GB/sec. General multi-core processing lands within the middle 50% band, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14736.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14693.2. Machine learning inference performance varies, delivering strong output on small 135M parameter models (263.31 tokens/sec text generation) but lower-quartile performance for 7B parameter prompt processing at 24.62 tokens/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a resource configuration suited for workloads where CPU processing density and fast storage access take precedence over vast memory footprints. The bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD eliminates network storage latency for scratch space and temporary file manipulation. Workload profiles that align with this architectural profile include software compilation pipelines, code testing, batch compression, intermediate ETL processing, and stateless web application serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM64 cloud instance equipped with 16 dedicated Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the system supplies 32.0 GB of RAM alongside 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect upper-quartile memory subsystem throughput, producing 307.54 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and fast single-threaded gzip compression at 33.08 GB/sec, while CPU compute metrics like Geekbench multi-core (14736.0) perform in the median range. By pairing 16 dedicated ARM cores with fast ephemeral NVMe disk space and reduced memory overhead, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for compute-centric workloads that require high local disk IOPS, including CI/CD build environments, batch data compression, and intermediate ETL stages.
